Ceiling fans are among the most frequently used appliances in Indian homes, particularly during the long summer months. With fans often running for several hours a day, their electricity consumption can make a noticeable difference to monthly power bills. This has made BLDC ceiling fans increasingly popular as an alternative to conventional induction-motor fans. BLDC stands for Brushless Direct Current. These fans use a brushless motor designed to deliver the required airflow while consuming less electricity. Regular ceiling fans generally use conventional induction motors, which have been the standard choice in Indian homes for decades. The biggest difference between the two is power consumption. A conventional ceiling fan can consume considerably more electricity than a comparable BLDC model while delivering similar everyday airflow. BLDC fans can therefore reduce running costs, although their higher purchase price means the savings need to be considered over the longer term. The right choice depends on how many hours the fan runs each day, the number of fans in your home and how long you expect to keep them. items.text: Binman settles debate on where batteries can be safely disposed of at home
items.article: A binman has issued a warning over the dangers of disposing of batteries at home due to fire risks - and has shared the correct disposal methods. After replacing old batteries, it can be all too easy to simply chuck them into your household rubbish . items.article: The 'Life in the UK' test is a key part of the British citizenship process One of the barriers to becoming a British citizen is the 'Life in the UK' test. It is a set of 24 questions which can be tricky even for those who have lived int he country their whole lives. According to the Office for National Statistics, 813,000 people immigrated to the UK in the year ending December 2025. The test is a mandatory requirement for migrants who have already come to the UK and are looking for Indefinite Leave to Remain or naturalisation as a British citizen. In order to be eligible to take the test, you must have no criminal convictions, have lived in the UK for a required length of time and demonstrate English language proficiency by passing a language test. Featuring a range of topics such as history, customs and culture, the test is made up of 24 questions. Those who take it have 45 minutes to complete it. While you can do the exam as much as you want, each attempt comes with a £50 fee, meaning you’d like to knock it out of the park on the first attempt to avoid the fees building up. In order to pass, you must answer 18 questions correctly, or 75%. Thankfully, the results are given immediately upon completion of the test, so you don’t have to wait to see how you fared.
